source_snapshot.title: Dubai government fees can now be paid in instalments with Tamara through the Dubai Payment System
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Finance and Dubai Digital announced the availability of Tamara, the leading platform in the field of deferred payments, as a payment option through the Dubai Payment System, in a move that gives customers more options when paying government service fees in instalments, and supports the Dubai government’s ongoing efforts to promote digital payments and provide a more flexible and convenient payment experience. Integrating Tamara into the Dubai Payments platform allows customers to manage their payments easily and transparently. Available instalment plans depend on customer eligibility, transaction type, and Tamara's terms and conditions. This step comes as part of the ongoing efforts of Dubai Finance and Digital Dubai to support the results of Dubai’s cashless strategy and to enhance the digital payments environment to meet the needs of individuals and various business sectors. His Excellency Abdulrahman Saleh Al Saleh, Director General of Dubai Finance, affirmed the department’s commitment to continuing to facilitate transactions for Dubai government customers by expanding the payment options available to them, noting that this is an important part of Dubai’s journey towards building an integrated digital financial system that prioritises ease and efficiency. His Excellency said that it is essential that customers be able to use these services with confidence, and be assured that their payments are processed in a secure environment. He added: “With the guidance of our wise leadership, and in cooperation with Dubai Digital and our partners in the public and private sectors, and in light of Dubai’s cashless strategy, we at Dubai Finance continue to develop the government payments system. Through these efforts, we are keen to keep pace with the rapid developments in payment technologies, and to provide solutions that contribute to simplifying transactions and enhancing the customer experience, in addition to supporting the efficiency and sustainability of the government collection system.” For his part, His Excellency Hamad Obaid Al Mansoori, Director General of Dubai Digital, said: “Dubai, with the vision of our wise leadership, is moving forward in building an integrated model for digital life, in which technology is part of people’s daily lives, and a means to enhance its ease, quality and efficiency. Digital payments represent one of the essential components of this model, with its role in supporting the digital economy, enhancing the efficiency of services and providing smoother and more flexible experiences for different segments of society.” His Excellency added: “The availability of Tamara within the Dubai Payment System embodies the approach based on integrating the roles of the public and private sectors, and benefiting from the innovations offered by the financial technology sector within a unified, reliable, secure and scalable digital system. We continue, in cooperation with Dubai Finance and our partners, to develop the shared digital infrastructure that enables government entities to adopt new solutions efficiently, and supports the achievements of Dubai’s cashless strategy and the journey of ‘digitising life in Dubai,’ thus enhancing Dubai’s position as a global capital of the digital economy.” Ahmed Ali Muftah, Executive Director of the Central Accounts Sector at Dubai Finance, said that adding Tamara to Dubai Payment comes as part of an ongoing effort to develop the system for collecting government service fees and to expand the digital payment options available to customers. He added: “The Dubai Payment platform enables government entities to collect their fees centrally through multiple payment channels. With the availability of more deferred payment options through the platform, these entities can also meet the needs of customers who prefer to pay fees in instalments. We continue to develop government revenue collection channels to keep pace with changing payment habits and customer expectations. As these channels develop, our priority remains to facilitate digital payments for customers, while maintaining a reliable and integrated payment environment for government entities that use the platform.” Amna Mohammed Lootah, Director of the Digital Payment Systems Regulation Department at Dubai Finance, said that making Tamara available within the channels for paying government transaction fees enables eligible customers to pay government fees in several instalments, stressing that diversifying payment methods is a key element in promoting the use of digital channels. She added: “We look at the payment journey from the customer’s perspective, and we believe that payment options should be clear to them, so that they can choose the payment method that best suits their needs.
